title: Fit a test's range to the tails
statement: Fit a test's floor and ceiling, and any items added to an adaptive bank, to where each grade's students sit, not to their average, which can hide either tail.
example: In one population, a grade's bottom quarter averaged 156.6 on the test's score scale, right at the bank's new floor.
detail: A per-grade baseline of a reading assessment's real population found one grade's bottom-quartile mean at RIT 156.6, exactly at the bank's expanded floor, and about a fifth of another grade above RIT 235, which the bank could not yet measure. The package made that table of tails its bank-expansion roadmap in place of an average that hides both edges, and the expansion added items at both ends.
against: The ceiling-side figure comes from the platform's own record slice, which the same document calls "a selected, high-achieving slice" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_CASE_FOR_APPROVAL.md`, line 40), so the full grade may sit lower; only the floor-side figure comes from the whole-population view. The ten-times floor is cited without a source link, and nothing here measures what a smaller bank would cost in precision or item exposure.

evidence.quote: And the tails table above is now the bank-expansion roadmap, not an average that hides both edges.
rpt2 shows the bottom-quartile G2 mean at RIT 156.6, exactly at the new floor
~20% of current G5 sit above even RIT 235; the bank cannot yet measure the top quintile of G5
+92 edge items (PR #30; floor to ~RIT 155, ceiling to 235)
Pool ratio stated both ways: 650/40 = 16.3× session length; against Stocking's recommended 10× floor (400 items), 1.6× — adequate, not lavish
Bank expansion priorities follow the population, not the average
The binding constraints are the edges, and the re-baselined population data says which edge binds where
